outcome: length and width of the free portion and penis root
cohort: The study included 39 human fetuses, 4 of whom had Prune Belly Syndrome, and the rest served as a control group.
finding: Fetuses with Prune Belly Syndrome showed no difference in penis total length but had a significant increase in total penile area, area of corpora cavernosa, and area of corpus spongiosum, suggesting an impact on penile development.
